explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates GPT-4 judgments against human evaluation on the same set of instances from the OKTest dataset, reporting that GPT-4's judgments closely approximate human judgments

prompts.notes: Full refusal/compliance classification prompt provided in Appendix A.3 with detailed rubric including full refusal, partial refusal, and compliance categories

guidelines.notes: Human evaluators used the same refusal/compliance classification criteria as GPT-4, with three individuals unrelated to the paper assessing refusal rates

sample_size.validated_by_both: subset of OKTest dataset (specific size not specified)
sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on a subset of the OKTest dataset containing safe questions with harmful words, tested on three models: LlaMa2-7B, Vicuna-7B, and Mistral-7B

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4's judgments closely approximate human judgments with quite high consistency, demonstrating reliable LLM-as-a-judge performance for refusal classification

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate refusal classification on the same instances. LLM additionally evaluates helpfulness on a 5-point scale, but human evaluation was only conducted for refusal classification.
